CORE-003.notes: RuntimeEvent envelope and 34 event families from DOMAIN.md §9; sequence assigned inside the commit transaction through a per-tenant counter row (concurrent writers serialize, rollback releases the value so the stream stays gap-free); mutation + event + outbox written atomically with NoEventStaged failing closed; outbox publishing behind an EventTransport trait with an explicit UnavailableTransport that never drops events silently; durable consumer cursors with resume. Reviewed and re-run on main (12 tests pass).

CORE-004.notes: WorkGraph/AgentGraph/StateGraph stores with cycle rejection (recursive reachability including parent_id), state-transition tables, revision compare-and-set, done only via mark_verification_passed, append-only attempts, and one atomic batch under a single graph revision. The delegation narrowing hook is a trait for RUN-005 rather than a second capability engine. Migration renumbered to 0003_graph_heads.sql during integration so migration versions stay unique; crate README trimmed to the documented length after the pipeline caught it.

CORE-005.notes: One transaction applies the graph batch under a single graph_heads compare-and-set and stages every RuntimeEvent (with tenant sequences and outbox rows) before one commit; a rejected change rolls back state and events together. Event mapping covers the DOMAIN §9.2 work/agent/run events named today and rejects unnamed change kinds with VALIDATION_SCHEMA before opening a transaction. PlanProposal application enforces base_revision, bounded size, acyclicity and the RUN-005 narrowing hook. One additive change in crates/events (commit_mutation_tx sharing the commit tail) so the two entry points cannot drift.

CORE-006.notes: ProtocolState per DOMAIN.md §5.7 with a pure next_safe_action precedence (cancel > reconcile unknown effect > approval > question > takeover handback > child > waits > continue); an unknown effect outcome is reconciled, never retried. Checkpoint metadata with generation and retention fencing. Stores take a caller-owned PgConnection so several writes compose into one transaction (the seam CORE-005 needs). Paths implemented as crates/server/src/runtime/{protocol_state,checkpoints}/ — equivalent to the task's crates/server/runtime/... mapping under this repository's src/ layout.

CORE-007.notes: Artifact/ArtifactVersion/Evidence/EvidenceBundle metadata with immutable evidence (insert-only, new identities per capture), tenant-prefixed content-addressed object keys verified by sha256, SigV4 S3 client with multipart upload and SSE-S3 against the real dev MinIO, fail-closed grants, and retention/legal-hold decisions recorded rather than silently deleting. Verification required two dev-stack fixes, both committed here: the generated .env now picks up settings added to config/dev.yaml (the MinIO SSE key previously stayed unset), and credentials stay stable across upgrades.

CORE-008.notes: Durable timers and a wait registry persisted in PostgreSQL (migration 0004) with exactly-once firing proven under two concurrent scheduler loops, survival across a pool drop/reconnect, fencing by generation, a typed saturated-queue error instead of silent drops, run dispatch through the canonical Run state machine, and routine due-time computation with skip/queue/catch_up_once absence policies. Integrated and re-verified by the principal agent after the delegating subagent was killed by a full disk.

CORE-009.notes: Rebuildable projections with a checkpoint per projection (deterministic incremental vs rebuilt state, idempotent re-application, crash/resume with no gaps or duplicates) and resumable client streaming per DOMAIN.md §9.3: durable event frames with cursors, transient live frames, channel and tenant scoping, and bounded backpressure that disconnects a slow consumer with a typed error. Integrated and re-verified by the principal agent after the subagent was killed by a full disk; the projections migration was renumbered to 0005 and the dev-dependency cycle the workspace gate caught was removed.

RUN-001.notes: Authoritative runtime: Run/Turn/Step/Attempt transitions evaluated inside the event-emitting transaction (illegal transitions roll back state and events together), generation fencing before any write, attempts appended never overwritten, cancellation and suspension as authoritative transitions, and recovery that applies next_safe_action (a WAITING_* run is released only by its matching resolution, an unsettled effect is reconciled never retried) and is idempotent across repeated calls. Turn-loop seams (model proposal, tool dispatch, delegation, verification) return typed not-available errors naming INT-002/RUN-011/RUN-002/RUN-008 rather than fabricating success. Two deviations are recorded: the runtime commits through EventStore::commit_mutation_tx instead of crates/graph because graph depends on the server's schema module (consolidation steps in HANDOFF.md), and the parity of both state tables with the database constraints is enforced by tests/architecture/test_runtime_state_parity.py added during integration. Also fixed a real CORE-006 defect found by the recovery test: cancellation_at is TIMESTAMPTZ and was decoded as a String.

RUN-002.notes: AgentThread lifecycle for teammates and workers on one primitive with a policy rule (teammates never JOIN, workers terminate only from JOINED), an exactly-once durable mailbox cursor, delegation that calls the narrowing check before any insert (a widening check writes nothing), handoff with a PENDING durable record that a restarted runtime can complete or roll back and that is idempotent when re-completed, and fanout join that parks the parent until the last child joins and never double-merges. During integration three follow-ups were added: the state-parity guard now covers AgentThreadStatus against the database constraint, DOMAIN §9.2 gained the two mailbox event names additively (agent.mailbox_delivered, agent.mailbox_cursor_advanced) so authority matches the contract, and the dev-stack integration test now runs in its own compose project on offset ports so its reset/volume teardown can no longer destroy a stack shared by other agents.

RUN-005.notes: Capability algebra composes grants by intersection with most-restrictive constraints (max_tier=min, approval only toward ask/never, earliest expiry, smallest budget) over all nine DOMAIN §6.1 selector kinds; projection assembly follows the fixed §6.2 layer order, ignores and records any widening as capability.widening_rejected naming the layer, and fails closed with an empty projection plus CAPABILITY_INPUTS_UNAVAILABLE when an input layer is unavailable or a policy has a gap at tier >= 1; authorize() always re-checks the current inputs digest and expiry so a stale projection cannot authorize dispatch; delegation narrowing is implemented for RUN-002's hook. During integration the architecture gate's new-persistent-store rule was corrected: capability owns capability_projections, so it is an allowed store owner, and the rule's fixtures now cover every table-owning module.
